title: Hazardous Products Act

officialOnlineCheck.result: No later amendment reported. Schedule 1 exclusions and Schedule 2 class names match official online text.

sourceHierarchy: This Act defines federally regulated hazardous products and the recognized classes. Hazardous Products Regulations SOR/2015-17 govern classification categories, criteria and hazard communication. UN GHS Rev.7 and adopted Rev.8 provisions are supporting technical sources; do not import unadopted classes.

importantSections.use: Definition of hazardous product (classified in a category/subcategory listed in Schedule 2 according to regulations); substance, mixture, manufactured article, sell, import, supplier, container and label.
Limits application of HPA Part II to sale or import of specified product types (also refers to Schedule 1).
Selling covered hazardous products generally requires a compliant supplier label and SDS, subject to specific legal exceptions.
Importing covered hazardous products generally requires a compliant supplier label and SDS, subject to specific legal exceptions.
Additional restrictions on sale/import of asbestos-containing hazardous products.
Prohibits misleading or false hazard labels, SDSs or other relevant hazard information.
Specified supplier records: true copies of label and SDS, acquisition/sales information; retention normally six years after the year to which they relate.
Regulatory power to establish categories and subcategories and prescribe classification, labels, SDS and exemptions.
Rules for incorporation of external materials, including incorporation as amended from time to time; verify incorporation language in each HPR rule.
Schedule 1 exclusions and Schedule 2 hazard classes may be amended by order.
Five groups to which Part II does not apply via section 12(j).
20 active physical and 12 active health hazard classes; one repealed physical entry 19.

scopeExclusions.interpretation: Exclusions relate to application of HPA Part II to the sale or importation of the described products. They do NOT prove a product is non-hazardous and do not determine unrelated occupational, transport or provincial duties.

section12Direct.wording: nuclear substance within the meaning of the Nuclear Safety and Control Act that is radioactive
hazardous product sold for recycling or recovery or intended for disposal
tobacco or a tobacco product as defined in section 2 of the Tobacco and Vaping Products Act

section12Direct.definition: HPA section 2; article formed to a specific shape/design, intended use depends in whole or part on that form, and no hazardous-product exposure under installation/normal use

schedule1.wording: Any pest control product as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Pest Control Products Act
Any explosive as defined in section 2 of the Explosives Act
Any cosmetic, device, drug or food, as defined in section 2 of the Food and Drugs Act
Any consumer product as defined in section 2 of the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act
Any wood or product made of wood

physical.name: Substances and mixtures which, in contact with water, emit flammable gases

health.name: Specific target organ toxicity — single exposure
Specific target organ toxicity — repeated exposure

schedule2.note: Schedule 2 lists classes only; adopted subcategories, cutoff values, evidence routes and classification methods must be sourced from the HPR. Explicit absence from HPA Schedule 2 is not an instruction to exclude environmental information from every SDS.

implementationRecommendations: Use the schedule2 active list as legally listed classes, NOT as proof the current pilot can assess each one.

Before a regulatory result, ask whether the user is evaluating supply/import for workplace use in Canada and whether section 12 or Schedule 1 excludes the product; allow an unknown/needing-legal-review status.
Do not call exempt products 'non-hazardous'; distinguish out of scope from not classified.
Do not use simple name keyword matching to determine exemptions that refer to definitions in other Acts.
Do not treat repealed Schedule 2 physical item 19 as an active hazard class.
Preserve supporting evidence and applicability decisions for audit trail; keep classification engine code unchanged until individual HPR pathways are validated.
Separate federal supplier HPA/HPR duties from provincial/territorial workplace obligations.
